subject: running individual bash chunks without knitting the entire script

messages.author: 6aa47051d60b80a6
messages.subject: running individual bash chunks without knitting the entire script
parts:
Hi there,

I just started using knitR.

I am using Rstudio (server) and when I run the  027-engine-bash.Rmd knitR example you provided and I run it all via the knitHTML button ( ctrl-shift-H) in Rstudio, everything runs like it should. However when I try to run the individual chunks as a single chunk I get errors.

When I for example run this chunk with "run current chunk" (ctrl alt C)

```{r test-bash, engine='bash'}
echo hello world
echo 'a b c' | sed 's/ /\|/g'
# number of lines
awk 'END{print NR;}' 027-engine-bash.Rmd
```

I get the following errors: 


> echo hello world
Error: unexpected symbol in "echo hello"
> echo 'a b c' | sed 's/ /\|/g'
Error: unexpected string constant in "echo 'a b c'"
> # number of lines
> awk 'END{print NR;}' 027-engine-bash.Rmd
Error: unexpected string constant in "awk 'END{print NR;}'"

R obviously tries to runs the chunk interpetting it as R code. Is this normal behaviour? And Is there a way to execute bash chunks, without knitting the entire script to html?

Thank you for your help

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] running individual bash chunks without knitting the entire script
parts:
Yes, this is normal, since RStudio does not support other languages.
It does not actually check the `engine` option in a code chunk. At the
moment, the only way to compile such a chunk is to compile the whole
document, but you are free to file a feature request to the RStudio
support forum: http://support.rstudio.com Thanks!

Regards,
Yihui
--
